params.prompt:
Create a grounded, cinematic scene about a business owner discovering how much her company still depends on her personally. The viewer should understand why an apparently healthy business may be difficult to sell.

An experienced woman who has run a profitable small business for twenty-five years is meeting a prospective male buyer at her place of business. The financial review has gone well. Begin with an ordinary, comfortable professional conversation between two people taking the business seriously. The buyer asks a practical question about how the business would run if she were away for a month. She begins to answer with the confidence of someone who knows her business, then stops as she realizes how much still relies on her. The buyer gives her room to think. Let that unfinished answer and the quiet realization carry the end of the scene.

Favor believable human attention, understated acting and a lived-in working environment. Choose natural staging and cinematic coverage that make the change in her understanding readable. Keep the same people and place coherent throughout. This is an illustrative enacted scene for an existing narrator-led film: conversational mouth movement is welcome, with no audible character dialogue, narration, music or on-screen text.
